extracted.intended_audience: librarians, faculty, researchers, and grantseekers (higher education and non-profit)
extracted.subtask_description: An annotated bibliography and reference guide listing directories, how-to books, agency manuals, databases, subject-specific sources, and newsletters to locate grant funding and to improve proposal writing and grant administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: BASIC GRANT DIRECTORIES
rubrics_metrics.description: Core, annually-updated directories and registers that list fellowship and grant support, arranged by discipline or program (examples: Annual Register of Grant Support; Directory of Research Grants; Foundation Directory; The Grants Register; Catalog of Federal Domestic Assistance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these as primary starting points. Example notes from the page: 'Directory of fellowship and grant support covering both public and private sources. Revised annually. Organized by discipline. One of the best places to start.'; 'Major source for government funding... This is the most comprehensive listing of federal programs and activities which provide assistance to the American public.'; 'The directory of American foundations... Lists over 3,000 foundations... Most important reference book on foundations in the U.S.'

rubrics_metrics.name: ADDITIONAL DIRECTORIES/BOOKS
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary directories, critiques, and thematic books that provide deeper context on foundations, fundraising realities, and specialized listings (examples cited include The Bread Game; Small Change From Big Bucks; Financial Aids for Higher Education Catalog; The College Blue Book).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult these for background, critiques of foundation behavior, or for specialized/larger-context reading: e.g., studies on why foundations fail to support social change, or collections aimed at smaller groups/newcomers.

rubrics_metrics.name: HOW-TO-DO-IT (practical guides to grantsmanship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical manuals on finding grants, writing proposals, budgeting, and administering awarded funds (examples: Getting Grants; Grants: How to Find Out About Them and What to Do Next; Grant Budgeting and Finance: Getting the Most Out of Your Grant Dollar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These contain hands-on advice such as budgeting, sample proposals, proposal-writing techniques and are recommended for practitioners. The bibliography flags certain titles as 'Excellent' or 'Good source' for practical steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOUNDATION GRANTS AND SOURCES — GENERAL
rubrics_metrics.description: National-level foundation reference works and indexes (examples: Foundation Directory; Foundation Grants Index; Foundation Grants to Individuals; National Databook; Foundation Fundamentals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to identify foundations by assets, giving patterns, subject/geographic focus, and to find foundations that fund individuals vs organizations. Notable guidance: 'Foundation Directory... Lists over 3,000 foundations that have assets of at least $1 million or make grants of $100,000 annually.'; 'FOUNDATION GRANTS TO INDIVIDUALS... Over 1,000 foundations that will make grants to individuals... Do not overlook this one.'; 'NATIONAL DATABOOK... Most comprehensive listing of grantmaking foundations available.'

rubrics_metrics.name: FOUNDATION GRANTS AND SOURCES — STATE (California example)
rubrics_metrics.description: State-level foundation and corporate giving directories and state records (examples: Guide to California Foundations; Registry of Charitable Trusts, State of California; Where the Money's At: How to Reach Over 500 California Grant-Making Foundations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult state-specific compilations and public records (e.g., registry filings) to identify local/regionally-focused funders and to inspect Form CT-2 filings where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOUNDATION GRANTS AND SOURCES — INTERNATIONAL
rubrics_metrics.description: Directories and guides covering foundations and grant-giving organizations outside the U.S. (examples: A Canadian Directory to Foundations; The International Foundation Directory; Philanthropic Foundations in Latin America).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use international directories compiled from questionnaires or regional studies to identify non-U.S. foundations and international grant opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: GOVERNMENT GRANTS AND SOURCES — GENERAL
rubrics_metrics.description: Government-wide compilations and primers on how to obtain government funding (examples: Catalog of Federal Domestic Assistance; How to Get Government Grants; U.S. Government Manual).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the Catalog of Federal Domestic Assistance and similar government compendia as the authoritative starting points for federal funding. The page notes these works describe programs, administering agencies, and which programs provide aid to non-governmental entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: GOVERNMENT — FEDERAL: AGENCY-SPECIFIC GUIDES AND MANUALS
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency manuals, factbooks and program guides that describe purposes, eligibility, characteristics, deadlines and administrative requirements for agency grant programs (examples: NIH Factbook; NIH Extramural Programs; NSF Guide to Programs; National Science Foundation Grant Administration Manual; Department of Health and Human Services Grants Administration Manual).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the relevant agency's program announcement, factbook, or administrative manual for authoritative information on eligibility, closing dates, program priorities and grant administration procedures. Example: 'This guide is designed to provide summary information about NSF programs. Describes basic purpose of each activity, characteristics, eligibility requirements and closing dates.'; 'This manual is intended to serve as a basic reference for those who are operationally engaged in the administrative and financial management of grants...'

rubrics_metrics.name: GOVERNMENT — STATE: INDIVIDUAL AGENCY GUIDELINES
rubrics_metrics.description: State agency program guidelines for specific grant programs (example entries: California Arts Council's Artists in Residence Grant Guidelines; Organizational Grant Guidelines; Performing Arts Touring Program: Grant Guidelines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the program-specific guidelines issued by state agencies for application requirements and program-specific objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: CORPORATE/BUSINESS GRANTS AND SOURCES
rubrics_metrics.description: Directories, surveys, and guides focused on corporate philanthropy and corporate-sponsored foundations (examples: Corporate 500: The Directory of Corporate Philanthropy; Corporate Foundation Profiles; Annual Survey of Corporate Contributions; Guide to Corporate Giving in the Arts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use corporate directories to learn policy statements, areas of interest, eligibility restrictions and sample grants; consult surveys and analyses to understand corporate giving trends and corporate foundations' profiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: COMMUNITY FOUNDATION GRANTS AND INFORMATION
rubrics_metrics.description: Information and handbooks on community foundations as local funding sources (examples: Community Foundations reprints; Handbook of Community Foundations: Their Formation, Development and Operation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat community foundations as distinct, locally-oriented funders; consult handbooks and Grantsmanship Center materials for formation, operation and grantmaking patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: SUBJECT SOURCES (general and discipline-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject- or discipline-specific funding guides and directories organized for fields such as the arts, humanities, sciences, education, health, microcomputers, museums, music, policy studies, languages, area studies, criminal justice, disability services, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use subject-specific bibliographies and directories (e.g., Grants in the Humanities; Grants for the Arts; Guide to Grants and Fellowships in Languages and Linguistics) to find funders and to obtain sample proposals and discipline-relevant advice. The page frequently notes that certain titles 'give a sample proposal' or 'contain information on writing the proposal.'

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSAL WRITING AND GRANTSMANSHIP
rubrics_metrics.description: Books and manuals focused on idea development, proposal drafting, proposal planning, sample proposals, and grantsmanship techniques (examples: Casebook of Grant Proposals in the Humanities; The New Grants Planner; Grant Writer's Handbook; The Quick Proposal Workbook; Successful Grantsmanship; The Grants Planner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult these for practical instruction on the process of developing ideas into fundable proposals, systems approaches to grantsmanship, sample proposals and commentary. The bibliography highlights volumes that reproduce successful proposals with commentary and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: FUND RAISING (development and donor relations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources focused on fundraising strategies, donor stewardship, and how to write fundraising letters and build development programs (examples: The Art of Fund Raising; Getting Your Share: An Introduction to Fund Raising; Handbook for Educational Fund Raising).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these when broader development or fundraising (beyond grantwriting) is relevant to securing institutional support or matching funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEWSLETTERS AND PERIODICALS
rubrics_metrics.description: Ongoing publications that report grant awards, program announcements, trends and practical advice (examples: Foundation News; Foundation Reporter; Grantsmanship Center News; Grants Magazine; Funding Sources Bulletin; Chronicle of Higher Education).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subscribe or consult back issues to track recently awarded grants, program changes, announcements, and articles on successful proposals and funder behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: INFORMATION/SUBSCRIPTION SERVICES
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial and curated information services and printouts that provide frequent, topical updates on foundation activity and funding opportunities (examples: TAFT Information Service — Foundation Reporter, Trustee of Wealth; Foundation Center printouts and profiles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use subscription services for current, frequently-updated data on foundations and philanthropic decision-makers; the bibliography notes services with update schedules (e.g., 'updated every 120 days').

rubrics_metrics.name: COMPUTERIZED SEARCH SERVICES/DATABASES
rubrics_metrics.description: Online and machine-searchable databases and retrieval systems for federal and foundation funding information (examples: Federal Assistance Program Retrieval System (FAPRS); Foundation Directory online/print with semiannual updates; Foundation Grants Index; Grants Database; Grants Database monthly updates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use computerized/online search tools where available for up-to-date, searchable access to grant program descriptions and recent awards. The page notes availability, update frequency, and that some government catalogs are now available on-line at selected sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: BIBLIOGRAPHIES
rubrics_metrics.description: Curated bibliographies and bibliographic guides collecting literature on philanthropy, grantseeking, fundraising and foundations (examples: Bibliography of Fund Raising and Philanthropy; Foundations and Fund Raising: A Bibliography of Books to 1980; Grants Resource Manual).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult bibliographies to identify further reading, foundational texts, and historical/background sources on philanthropy and grantsmanship.
